securitylake/create-data-lake.rst.Example 1: To configure your data lake i: Security Lake creates its buckets and names them aws-security-data-lake-<region>-<id>, so the bucket names show the real format. Example 1 is titled 'To configure your data lake in multiple Regions'. Its --configurations sets up us-east-1 and us-east-2, and the output in both examples shows a rollup (replicationConfiguration) to ap-northeast-3 with an ap-northeast-3 roleArn. The scenario needs several Regions, so us-west-2 alone would break it.

securitylake/list-data-lakes.rst.To list the Security Lake configuration: Security Lake creates its buckets and names them aws-security-data-lake-<region>-<id>, so the bucket names show the real format. The output shows a data lake in us-east-1 that rolls up to a second Region (replicationConfiguration regions ap-northeast-3, with an ap-northeast-3 roleArn). Cross-Region replication needs two different Regions, so the file cannot use us-west-2 alone.

securitylake/update-data-lake.rst.Example 1: To update your data lake sett: Security Lake creates its buckets and names them aws-security-data-lake-<region>-<id>, so the bucket names show the real format. Same content as create-data-lake. Example 1 updates the data lake in two Regions (us-east-1 and us-east-2), and the description mentions rollup Region settings. Both outputs replicate to ap-northeast-3. Multi-Region and rollup-Region replication cannot be shown with one Region.

ssm/describe-effective-patches-for-patch.Example 1: To get all patches defined by: Example 2 has to pass the full ARN of an AWS managed patch baseline (arn:aws:ssm:us-east-2:733109147000:patchbaseline/pb-020d361a05defe4ed), and the text says so explicitly. 733109147000 is the AWS-owned account that publishes the predefined baselines in us-east-2. Both the account and the pb- ID differ by region, so swapping in 123456789012 or us-west-2 would either make it look like a customer-owned baseline or produce an ARN that does not exist.

ssm/describe-patch-baselines.rst.Example 1: To list all patch baselines: The output lists the AWS-provided predefined baselines (AWS-SuseDefaultPatchBaseline, AWS-DefaultPatchBaseline). Their BaselineId ARNs belong to the AWS-owned account 733109147000 in us-east-2, and that account and the pb- IDs differ by region. Replacing them would either show AWS-owned baselines as belonging to the customer or produce ARNs that do not exist.

ssm/register-default-patch-baseline.rst.To set the default patch baseline: The second example registers the AWS-provided CentOS predefined patch baseline by its real ARN, arn:aws:ssm:us-east-2:733109147000:patchbaseline/pb-0574b43a65ea646ed. AWS owns that account, and the baseline ID is specific to that region. Swapping in placeholders would point to a baseline that does not exist.
